items.question: How do I create an account?
items.answer: Click Get started free on the home page. Fill in your name and email. Then pick a password of at least 8 characters.

items.question: Can I use an email that is already registered?
items.answer: No. The form will ask you to log in instead.

items.question: Can I change my name?
items.answer: Yes. Edit your first or last name in Settings and select Save changes. The sidebar shows the new name straight away.

items.question: Can I change my email address?
items.answer: Not from Settings. Your email is how you sign in and it stays fixed. Contact the team if it needs to change.

items.question: What happens when I delete my account?
items.answer: You are logged out and lose access straight away. Your data is kept in case you change your mind.

items.question: Can I get my account back after deleting it?
items.answer: Yes. Log in with the same email and password, then choose Recover account. If you use Google, sign in with Google and choose Recover with Google.

items.question: How do I log in?
items.answer: Open the login page and enter your email and password. Click Log in to reach your dashboard.

items.question: I forgot my password. What now?
items.answer: Click Forgot password? on the login page. We will email you a link to set a new one.

items.question: How do I change my password?
items.answer: Open the Security card in Settings and select Change password. Enter your current password first, then type the new one twice. Your other devices are signed out when it changes.

items.question: I sign in with Google. Can I change my password here?
items.answer: No. Your password belongs to your Google account. Change it with Google instead, using the link in Settings.

items.question: How do I log out?
items.answer: Use the Logout button at the bottom of the sidebar. Settings has one as well.

items.question: Why was I sent back to the login page?
items.answer: Your session ended. Log in again to carry on where you left off.

items.question: Can I use two accounts at the same time?
items.answer: Yes. Each browser tab keeps its own login.

items.question: Can I log out of every device at once?
items.answer: Yes. In Settings, open the Security card and select Sign out everywhere. Every session ends, including the one you are using.

items.question: Does OptiGrid have a dark mode?
items.answer: Yes. Open Settings and pick Dark in the Appearance card. The change happens straight away.

items.question: Is my theme saved?
items.answer: It is. Your choice is saved to your account and follows you when you log in on another device.

items.question: What does the System theme do?
items.answer: It copies the setting on your device. When your device switches to dark mode at night, OptiGrid switches with it.

items.question: Can I turn animations off?
items.answer: Yes. Under Motion in the Appearance card, choose Reduce. Charts appear at once and the 3D model holds still.

items.question: What does Match device do for motion?
items.answer: OptiGrid follows the reduced motion setting on your computer or phone. Pick Full if you want animations even when your device asks for less.

items.question: Do my other display choices follow me to other devices?
items.answer: Only your theme does, because it is saved to your account. Every other display choice stays on the device where you set it. A phone on mobile data and an office desktop rarely need the same settings.

items.question: How do I make OptiGrid use less data?
items.answer: Open Settings and set Live updates to Data saver. Live streams close and pages check for new readings four times less often.

items.question: What happens when I pause live updates?
items.answer: Pages stop refreshing on their own. A banner at the top of each page reminds you and offers Resume live updates. Anomaly alerts still come through.

items.question: The Live page says Updates paused. Is something wrong?
items.answer: No. Live updates are paused in Settings on this device. Resume them from the banner or pick Normal again in Settings.

items.question: The 3D view is slow on my laptop. What can I do?
items.answer: Set 3D graphics to Battery saver in Settings. The building model then draws at a lower resolution and holds still between readings. The heatmap gets lighter too.

items.question: What does Auto do for 3D graphics?
items.answer: It starts at full sharpness and lowers the resolution whenever your device struggles to keep up. Most people can leave it there.

items.question: Can I change how dates and numbers look?
items.answer: Yes. Pick a Region format in the Dates and numbers card in Settings. With South Africa chosen, 12480.5 shows as 12 480,5.

items.question: How do I switch to a 24-hour clock?
items.answer: Choose 24-hour under Clock in Settings. Times on every page change straight away.

items.question: What does the Default region format do?
items.answer: Every screen keeps the format it used before. Most numbers then follow the language set in your browser.

items.question: Can I see the data OptiGrid keeps about me?
items.answer: Yes. Open Settings and select Download my data. A file with the personal information we hold about you downloads at once.

items.question: Why does OptiGrid offer this download?
items.answer: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) gives you the right to know what we hold about you. The download makes that quick.

items.question: How do I open the file?
items.answer: It is a JSON file. Any text editor can open it.

items.question: Is my password in the file?
items.answer: No. Passwords are never kept in a form anyone can read. The file leaves them out.

items.question: How do I add a building?
items.answer: Click + Add building on the dashboard. Only the name is required.

items.question: What does the Validate button do?
items.answer: It looks up the address you typed. The latitude and longitude are then filled in for you.

items.question: Why should I add the floor area?
items.answer: Energy use is compared per square metre. Without a floor area the building is left out of that comparison.

items.question: What is the 3D view?
items.answer: Open any building to see a model of it. Each sensor sits in its zone and glows with its live load.

items.question: How do I add a sensor?
items.answer: Open the building and click Sensors. Use Register sensor to add a new one.

items.question: What does the Live page show?
items.answer: It shows how much power each building is using right now. You can also see the energy used so far today.

items.question: Why is a building marked Offline?
items.answer: No reading has arrived from it in the last five minutes.

items.question: Is there a video guide?
items.answer: Yes. The Help Centre has short tutorials. There is one for the heatmap and one for the 3D view.

items.question: What does Towers do?
items.answer: It turns each site into a 3D column. A taller tower means the site uses more energy.

items.question: What does the heatmap show?
items.answer: Your buildings on a map. Sites that use more energy stand out in a stronger colour.

items.question: Can I look at the past or the future?
items.answer: Yes. Drag the timeline to look back up to 90 days. You can also look up to 90 days ahead.

items.question: Why is my building missing from the map?
items.answer: It has no location yet. Edit the building and use Validate on its address.

items.question: How do I compare two buildings?
items.answer: Open Compare and pick a building in each box. Choose a date range and whether to compare cost or energy.

items.question: Why is there no efficiency ratio?
items.answer: Both buildings need a floor area for this number to work.

items.question: How do I run a forecast?
items.answer: The Forecast page runs a 7 day forecast for your busiest building as soon as it opens. For another building, pick it with a horizon and click Run forecast.

items.question: What is the difference between weekly and monthly?
items.answer: Weekly shows the next seven days hour by hour. Monthly covers the next twelve weeks.

items.question: What is the shaded band on the chart?
items.answer: It is the range the real demand will most likely fall in. A wide band means the forecast is less certain.

items.question: How accurate is the forecast?
items.answer: Look at the MAPE figure below the chart. A lower number means a closer forecast.

items.question: What are insights?
items.answer: Tips for moving load to cheaper hours. Each one shows the monthly saving in Rand.

items.question: Can I approve an insight?
items.answer: Building managers and administrators can approve or dismiss them. Viewers can still read every one.

items.question: What is the Savings level slider?
items.answer: It lets you choose between saving more and keeping staff comfortable. The Sweet spot mark is a good place to start.

items.question: What is an anomaly alert?
items.answer: A warning that a reading is outside its normal range.

items.question: What should I do when I get one?
items.answer: First check for a known reason like work on site. If there is none, let the building manager know.

items.question: Can I close an alert?
items.answer: Building managers can open an alert and choose Resolve or Ignore.

items.question: Can I change when alerts are raised?
items.answer: Yes. Building managers can set their own limits with Configure Threshold.

items.question: What does the ESG page show?
items.answer: A tree that reflects your building's health score. It grows fuller as the score goes up.

items.question: What do the sliders do?
items.answer: They let you test a change before you make it. Reset to Baseline puts everything back.

items.question: What is in the compliance report?
items.answer: A summary of last month's energy use in line with ISO 50001. You can download it as a PDF or a JSON file.

items.question: What does Verify Data Integrity do?
items.answer: It checks that no record was changed after it was saved.

items.question: Who can change tariff rates?
items.answer: Only administrators can. Rates are set for each season and time of day.

items.question: What is OptiGrid?
items.answer: An energy platform for people who run more than one building. It shows where your energy goes and how to use less.

items.question: Who is it for?
items.answer: Facility teams and building owners who want to cut energy costs.

items.question: What do I need to get started?
items.answer: Your buildings need meters or sensors that send readings. Everything else is set up in the app.

items.question: Which currency does it use?
items.answer: All costs are shown in South African Rand.

items.question: How do I create an account?
items.answer: Click Get started free. Fill in your name and email and pick a password.

items.question: I forgot my password. What now?
items.answer: Click Forgot password? on the login page. We will email you a link to set a new one.

items.question: Do I need to install anything?
items.answer: No. OptiGrid runs in your web browser.

items.question: Can I see readings as they happen?
items.answer: Yes. The Live page updates every few seconds.

items.question: Can I see my buildings on a map?
items.answer: Yes. A heatmap shows which sites use the most energy. You can also look back or ahead in time.

items.question: Is there a 3D view?
items.answer: Each building has a 3D model with its sensors placed inside.

items.question: Can OptiGrid predict demand?
items.answer: It can. Forecasts reach up to twelve weeks ahead.

items.question: Can I compare buildings?
items.answer: Pick any two and compare their cost or energy over time.

items.question: Does it work on a slow connection?
items.answer: Yes. Turn on Data saver in Settings and pages check for new readings less often. Older laptops can also use a lighter 3D mode.

items.question: How will I know if something is wrong?
items.answer: OptiGrid raises an alert when a reading looks unusual.

items.question: Will it help me save money?
items.answer: Yes. It suggests moving load to cheaper hours and shows what you would save.

items.question: Does OptiGrid change anything on site by itself?
items.answer: No. Your team decides what to act on.

items.question: Can I get reports for an audit?
items.answer: You can download an ISO 50001 report with a digital signature.

items.question: What is the ESG score?
items.answer: A score from 0 to 100 for how green a building runs. Sliders let you test changes before you make them.

items.question: Can different people see different things?
items.answer: Yes. What you see depends on your role.

items.question: How do I contact the team?
items.answer: Use the Contact link at the bottom of the page.

items.question: Can I get a copy of my data?
items.answer: Yes. After you log in, open Settings and select Download my data.
